skill.name: backend-dev-guidelines
skill.description: Backend development guidance for Node.js, Express, and TypeScript services. It covers layered architecture, controllers, services, repositories, Zod validation, Prisma access, Sentry monitoring, configuration, async patterns, and tests.
skill.summary: Guide backend teams through consistent Node.js, Express, TypeScript, Prisma, Sentry, and Zod service patterns.
skill.author: BrianDai22

security_audit.summary: Static findings are overwhelmingly false positives caused by Markdown examples, relative TypeScript imports, template literals, placeholder URLs, and configuration documentation. No prompt injection, malware intent, external command execution, or host environment access was found. One semantic privacy issue remains because the Sentry guidance recommends broad mandatory request capture without complete body and query scrubbing.

remediation.issue: Sentry request capture may collect sensitive user data.
remediation.suggestion: Disable request data, headers, query strings, and IP capture by default, or show an allowlist with full body and query scrubbing.

remediation.issue: Development secret defaults can be copied into production.
remediation.suggestion: Gate local defaults by environment and fail startup when JWT, session, database, or Sentry secrets are missing outside development.

semantic_findings.title: Telemetry May Capture Sensitive Request Data
semantic_findings.description: The monitoring guide makes Sentry capture mandatory and enables request bodies, headers, IP addresses, query strings, URLs, and user email fields. The shown sanitizer removes only authorization and cookie headers and masks one email field, so sensitive request data may still leave the service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited Sentry configuration explicitly includes broad request data and only partially scrubs sensitive fields. This is a clear privacy risk if users copy the guidance into production services.

content.value_statement: Backend teams need consistent patterns for APIs, services, validation, and monitoring. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for Node.js and TypeScript services.
actual_capabilities: Explains a layered route, controller, service, and repository architecture for Express services.
Provides BaseController patterns for consistent responses, errors, logging, and Sentry capture.
Shows Zod validation patterns for request bodies, parameters, query strings, and DTOs.
Documents Prisma repository, transaction, pagination, caching, and testing patterns.
Guides configuration migration toward centralized unifiedConfig usage.
Includes refactoring examples for moving large route handlers into services.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not inspect a live codebase by itself.
Examples must be adapted to each service, schema, and deployment environment.
It does not verify database migrations, Prisma models, or runtime permissions.
Monitoring and secrets examples need security review before production use.

use_cases.title: Create a New API Feature
use_cases.description: Use the route, controller, service, repository, validation, and test checklists to build a feature with consistent structure.

use_cases.title: Refactor Large Route Files
use_cases.description: Use the anti-pattern examples and extraction guide to move business logic from routes into controllers and services.

use_cases.title: Standardize Service Practices
use_cases.description: Use the configuration, middleware, monitoring, and async guidance to align multiple TypeScript microservices.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Backend Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the backend-dev-guidelines skill to plan a new Express API feature. Include routes, controller methods, service logic, validation, database access, monitoring, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Design Controller and Service Layers
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the routing, controller, service, and repository guidance to this endpoint. Keep routes thin, validate input with Zod, and describe error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Route Anti-Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this route handler with the backend-dev-guidelines skill. Identify business logic, database access, and validation that should move to controller, service, or repository layers.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Microservice Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the full backend-dev-guidelines skill to audit this service structure. Check architecture, async handling, Sentry coverage, unifiedConfig usage, Prisma access, validation, and tests.

output_examples.input: Plan a user profile update endpoint.
output: Suggested route and controller responsibilities for the profile update flow.
Service and repository boundaries for validation, permissions, and database updates.
Test coverage notes for success, validation failure, not found, and permission cases.

output_examples.input: Refactor a route that contains workflow logic and Prisma calls.
output: A short issue list showing why the route is too large.
A proposed controller, service, and repository split.
Migration steps that preserve behavior while improving testability.

output_examples.input: Review configuration and monitoring patterns for a service.
output: A checklist for centralized configuration, required secret validation, and local defaults.
A Sentry review covering error capture, context, privacy controls, and performance spans.

best_practices: Use the resource files progressively, starting with the specific backend task you are doing.
Ask for a layer-by-layer plan before generating controller, service, repository, or middleware code.
Review generated monitoring and secrets handling with production security requirements before adoption.
anti_patterns: Do not copy examples without adapting service names, schemas, permission checks, and deployment settings.
Do not keep business logic, validation, and database access inside route files.
Do not enable broad error telemetry without explicit PII and secret scrubbing.

faq.question: What type of projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Node.js, Express, and TypeScript backend services that use layered architecture and Prisma-style data access.

faq.question: Can it generate complete backend files?
faq.answer: It can guide file structure and implementation patterns, but users must adapt generated code to their service.

faq.question: Does it require Prisma?
faq.answer: Many examples use Prisma, but the repository and service patterns can be adapted to other data layers.

faq.question: Does it cover testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for unit tests, integration tests, mocking, coverage goals, and route testing.

faq.question: Does it manage secrets safely?
faq.answer: It discusses centralized configuration and gitignore rules, but production secret handling still needs review.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
